sentences.text: Yixianopterus is a pterosaur genus with an elongated, flat skull measuring approximately 25 centimeters in length.
Its wings were relatively long and robustly built, featuring a short fourth metacarpal bone and a deltopectoral crest extending 25.38 mm, resulting in an estimated wingspan of about 3.5 meters.
The teeth were subequal with a diastema increasing posteriorly, and the jaw ended in a blunt tip with short front teeth perpendicular to the jawline.
An outline of the head preserved in the sediment showed a distinct dorsal inclination.
Measurements of the leg bones reveal a metatarsal III of 28.19 mm and a preserved tibia portion of 102.63 mm.
The genus is known from a single holotype specimen, JZMP-V-12, found in the uppermost Jinggangshan bedding of the Yixian Formation.
This bedding consists of basaltic and siliciclastic sediments and is now housed at the Benxi Geological Museum.
Researchers suggest that due to its large wings and elongated head, Yixianopterus was likely a specialized glider that fed on fish.
Lü et al. (2006) assigned Yixianopterus to the family Lonchodectidae based on dental characters and bone ratio comparisons.

Later, Martill (2011) considered it potentially related to Unwindia, while Witton (2013) assigned it to the family Ornithocheiridae, but a reappraisal by Jiang et al. (2020) recovered it as a basal member of the clade Istiodactyliformes.
Yixianopterus lived from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago, in a marine environment with significant volcanic activity.
It is debated whether Avgodectes, usually considered an embryo, might be a juvenile Yixianopterus, which would give the first name priority.
